questions.0.explain.t: CWPP complements CSPM: one looks at the environment, the other looks at what runs inside it.

questions.0.options.0.t: The running workload: VMs, containers and functions, seeing behavior at runtime

questions.0.options.1.t: Only the configuration of the accounts and managed services

questions.0.options.2.t: The source code stored in the organization's repositories

questions.0.options.3.t: The public DNS and the company's domain records

questions.1.explain.t: Anomalous behavior during execution is what CWPP and tools like Falco observe.

questions.1.options.0.t: A container opening a reverse shell to an external IP

questions.1.options.1.t: A bucket with a restrictive policy and private access

questions.1.options.2.t: An image that is signed and verified before it runs

questions.1.options.3.t: A role that requires MFA to be assumed by people

questions.1.q.t: Which signal is typical of runtime detection?

questions.2.explain.t: Knowing what is normal for a workload makes the abnormal visible.

questions.2.options.0.t: Because deviations from normal stand out and produce more precise alerts

questions.2.options.1.t: Because it removes the need to keep workload logs

questions.2.options.2.t: Because it automatically encrypts the traffic between containers

questions.2.options.3.t: Because it replaces IAM in deciding who accesses what

questions.2.q.t: Why does a behavior baseline help?
